svg.title: What the Encoder Actually Looks Like
svg.desc: Reference photographs © Pololu Corporation — pololu.com. RoboLore Lesson 6 follow-up graphic showing the Zumo encoder hardware and a bare micro metal gearmotor. Both authentic Pololu JPEG photographs are embedded byte-for-byte under separate xlink:href attributes. Live vector labels explain the magnet disc, Hall-effect sensors, gearmotor, output shaft, 75.81:1 gearbox, motor can, and extended rear shaft, and show how 12 counts per motor rotation becomes approximately 74.3 counts per centimeter.
svg.text: What the Encoder Actually Looks Like
Close-up view — magnet disc and Hall-effect sensors

g.text: times for every one turn of
909.7 counts over 122.5 mm (12.25 cm) = ~74.3 counts / cm
the magnet disc presses onto THIS

svg.text: One turn of the wheel is 75.81 turns of the magnet. That is where 909.7 comes from.
The encoder is a small system made of a magnet disc plus nearby Hall sensors.
It is not hidden entirely inside the motor can.
As the shaft turns, the magnet passes the sensors and creates counts.
